  1. Disk at 97% says the bottleneck is paging, not a shortage of ready work.
  2. Adding a process would take frames from the ones already starved and raise the fault rate further.
  3. Suspending a process returns its frames, letting the survivors reach their working sets.
  4. Hence (B) is the correct action.

Answer: Option (B).

Why the other options are wrong.

  • (A) is exactly the feedback loop that causes thrashing.
  • (C) changes granularity without adding frames and can increase internal fragmentation.
  • (D) reduces table size, not the frame deficit.

Common misconception. Reading “CPU idle” as “add work”. That inference is valid only when the disk is also idle.

Takeaway. CPU low + disk low → add processes. CPU low + disk high → remove processes.

questions.subject: operating-systems
questions.question: Which of the following statements about page-fault-frequency (PFF) control and working-set control are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)
questions.question_html: Which of the following statements about page-fault-frequency (PFF) control and working-set control are TRUE? (Select all that apply.)
options: Under PFF control, a process whose fault rate exceeds the upper bound is given additional frames.
Under PFF control, a process whose fault rate falls below the lower bound may have frames taken away.
If a process needs more frames and none are free, the system may suspend another process or swap one out.
Both schemes require the operating system to know each process's future reference string.
options_html: Under PFF control, a process whose fault rate exceeds the upper bound is given additional frames.
Under PFF control, a process whose fault rate falls below the lower bound may have frames taken away.
If a process needs more frames and none are free, the system may suspend another process or swap one out.
Both schemes require the operating system to know each process's future reference string.
questions.solution_html:
Concept. Both schemes measure demand and allocate frames to match it. PFF watches the fault rate directly and keeps it inside a band; the working-set model computes WSSi from the last Δ references and allocates that many frames.

Step by step.

  1. PFF: rate above the upper bound means the process needs more frames, so (A) is true.
  2. PFF: rate below the lower bound means it holds more than it needs, so frames may be reclaimed — (B) is true.
  3. Frames are finite; when the demand cannot be met, the system reduces the degree of multiprogramming — (C) is true.
  4. Both use recent history, never the future, so (D) is false.

Answer: Options (A), (B) and (C).

Why the other options are wrong.

  • (D) describes OPT-style replacement, which needs the future and cannot be implemented online. PFF and working-set control are both online.

Common misconception. Assuming PFF only ever adds frames. It is a two-sided controller: the lower bound exists precisely so that frames can be reclaimed and shared.

Takeaway. PFF: a band on the fault rate. Working set: a window on the references. Both allocate frames from history.

questions.subject: operating-systems
questions.question:
A process references the pages 2, 6, 1, 2, 4, 2, 6, 1, 2, 3. Using the working-set model with window Δ = 5, how many pages are in the working set at time t = 10, that is, after the tenth reference?
(Enter an integer.)
questions.question_html:
A process references the pages 2, 6, 1, 2, 4, 2, 6, 1, 2, 3. Using the working-set model with window Δ = 5, how many pages are in the working set at time t = 10, that is, after the tenth reference?
(Enter an integer.)
questions.solution_html:
Concept. The working set at time t is the set of distinct pages referenced in the window of the last Δ references, counting the current one. Repeated references add nothing to a set.

Step by step.

  1. Take the last five references, positions 6 to 10: 2, 6, 1, 2, 3.
  2. Form the set: {2, 6, 1, 3}.
  3. Page 2 appears twice but is counted once.
  4. |W(10)| = 4, so the process needs four frames to hold its working set.

Answer: 4.

Common misconception. Reporting 5 because the window is five references wide, or sliding the window one position too far and including 4. The window always ends at the current reference.

Takeaway. Working-set size = number of distinct pages in the window, which is at most Δ and usually less.
